items.titleZh: 迈凯伦在巴库推出全新车身套件
items.summaryZh: 迈凯伦在阿塞拜疆大奖赛推出近乎全新的车身套件，重点包括侧箱、侧箱进气口、引擎盖和进气箱/防滚架整流罩。此举旨在提升直线速度，因为巴库赛道直线速度对圈速至关重要。

media.altZh: 迈凯伦在巴库推出全新车身套件

items.originalTitle: Where McLaren's been brutal with big F1 body package change
items.summaryEn: McLaren has introduced an almost complete new body package for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with the most visible changes being the sidepods, sidepod intakes, engine cover, and airbox intake/rollover bar fairing. The update aims to improve straightline speed, which is crucial for lap time in Baku.
detailZh: 迈凯伦继续推进升级，在巴库出现了一些视觉上引人注目的发展。为阿塞拜疆大奖赛，它引入了或多或少全新的车身套件，其中最显眼的元素是侧箱、侧箱进气口、引擎盖以及进气箱进气口/防滚架整流罩的轮廓。
在新规下，它在效率方面一直挣扎。迈凯伦在直线速度方面很少能名列前茅，所以我相当确定这个套件是为巴库匆忙推出的——因为在那里，直线速度是圈速的主要推动因素。
从散热器进气口开始，迈凯伦在这里偏离了常规。如果说有什么相似的话，它走了与奥迪自赛季初以来一直采用的类似路线。
这是一个相当粗暴的改变，你可以称之为硬加上去的封闭面板。主要原因是侧箱的这一部分包含了侧撞结构，并与生存单元粘合，所以要完全改变它并不容易，或者在预算帽下，也不便宜。
然而，如果它能提升赛车性能，那么最好还是把它装上，忍受可能的评论（比如我的），并尽可能收获圈速上的好处。
用洋红色标出的进气口区域在开放面积方面相当相似，但进入该区域的气流来自上游一个非常不同的位置。像大多数车队一样，迈凯伦加载前翼的外侧部分，就在内轮罩/刹车导管内表面内侧。开口位置的这种变化意味着，为了获得所需平衡而加载前翼时，对冷却的影响不会那么大。
这也让迈凯伦得以修改看不见的冷却系统。我推测它把散热器芯向前移动了。侧箱侧面轮廓的这种变化将更早地引发更多下洗。
侧箱的改变也让迈凯伦得以修改出口百叶窗。很难说程度如何，因为这些通常取决于赛道。慢速、炎热的赛道意味着赛车需要更多冷却。巴库有不错的直道和高速，意味着冷却不那么困难。
进气箱进气口从更接近椭圆形改为三角形，同样符合冷却需求。正如我常说的，用于冷却的气流在产生下压力方面是浪费的。然而，如果一些所需的冷却气流从侧箱进气口转移到了进气箱进气口，那么在这些损失方面可能就不那么剧烈。
与进气箱进气口的变化一致，迈凯伦还改动了用紫色标出的引擎盖鳍片。旧版鳍片上缘的这些台阶会在赛车于弯中偏航时产生涡流。
这些涡流是帮助还是妨碍后翼性能，取决于数小时的CFD建模和可能的风洞测试。它们的需求也取决于后翼配置。
后轮前方的区域也有小的细节变化。这个区域对入洗和出洗的量至关重要。你能产生的出洗越多，底板密封就越好，进而扩散器性能就越好。
这些发展如何提升了整车的效率，将很有趣。迈凯伦能否在巴库为这些慢弯运行更高的下压力水平，同时减少其直线速度劣势？
巴库绝对是那种你会很快找到答案的赛道。
detailEn: McLaren continues to push on with upgrades, with some visually striking developments appearing in Baku. For the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, it has introduced more or less a complete new body package, the most visible elements of which are the sidepods, sidepod intakes, engine cover and the profile of the airbox intake/rollover bar fairing.

It has struggled with these new regulations in terms of efficiency. McLaren has very seldom been up there as far as straightline speed is concerned, so I'm pretty sure this package was rushed through for Baku - as straightline speed there is a prime mover as far as laptime is concerned.
Starting with the radiator intakes, McLaren has gone off the beaten track here. If anything, it has gone down a similar route to what Audi has been running since the start of the season.

It's a fairly brutal change and you might call it a bodged-on blanking panel. The main reason for this is that this section of the sidepod incorporates the side-impact structure and is bonded to the survival cell, so to completely change that is not easy or, working within the budget cap, cheap.
However, if it improves the performance of the car, then it is better to get it on there, suffer the potential remarks (like mine) and reap any benefit in laptime possible.

The intake area highlighted in magenta is fairly similar as far as the open area is concerned, but the airflow into that area is coming from a very different place upstream. As most teams do, McLaren loads up the outer section of the front wing just inside the inner wheel fairing/brake duct inner surface. This change in the opening position will mean that loading up the front wing as required to get the balance required won't affect the cooling quite as much.
This has also allowed McLaren to revise the unseen cooling system. I would assume it has moved the radiator cores forward. This change in sidepod side profile will induce more downwash earlier.

This sidepod change has also allowed it to revise the outlet louvres. It's difficult to say to what extent, as these are normally circuit-dependent. Slow, hot circuits mean the car needs more cooling. Baku has decent straights with high top speeds, meaning that cooling is not quite so difficult.

The change to the airbox intake from more of an ellipse to a triangular shape is again in line with cooling requirements. As I often say, airflow used for cooling is wasted as far as producing downforce is concerned. However, if some of the required cooling airflow has been moved from the sidepod intake to the airbox intake, then it is probably less dramatic as far as those losses are concerned.

In line with that airbox intake change, McLaren has also altered the engine cover fin, which is highlighted in purple. These steps on the upper edge of the older version of the fin would generate vortices when the car is in yaw mid-corner.

Whether these vortices help or hinder the rear wing performance is down to hours and hours of CFD modelling and probably tunnel testing. Their requirement will also be dependent on rear wing configuration.

There are also small detail changes to the area in front of the rear tyre. This area is critical to the amount of inwash and outwash. The more outwash you can generate, the better the sealing of the underfloor and, in turn, the better the performance of the diffuser.

It will be interesting to see how these developments have improved the efficiency of the overall car. Can McLaren run a higher downforce level for these slow corners in Baku while reducing its straightline deficit?
Baku is definitely the circuit where you will find out very quickly.
keyPointsZh: 散热器进气口设计偏离常规，类似奥迪本赛季初的路线，被形容为粗暴的封闭面板改装。
侧箱变化允许修改冷却系统和出口百叶窗，并可能将散热器芯前移。
进气箱从椭圆形改为三角形，引擎盖鳍片也调整，以优化冷却和减少涡流。
keyPointsEn: The radiator intake design deviates from convention, similar to Audi's approach since the start of the season, described as a brutal blanking panel modification.
The sidepod changes allow for revised cooling system and outlet louvres, and may have moved radiator cores forward.
The airbox intake changed from an ellipse to a triangular shape, and the engine cover fin was altered to optimize cooling and reduce vortices.

items.titleZh: F1车手准备迎接巴库站“极其不自然”的驾驶挑战
items.summaryZh: F1车手预计巴库站将暴露2026年赛车需要更多“极其不自然”驾驶方式的问题，车手对能量部署缺乏控制，并担忧排位赛和正赛中的极端速度差可能带来危险。
items.originalTitle: F1车手准备迎接巴库站“极其不自然”的驾驶挑战
items.summaryEn: F1 drivers expect Baku to expose the need for more "super unnatural" driving of the 2026 cars, with drivers having no control over energy deployment and fearing dangerous closing speeds in qualifying and the race.
detailZh: F1车手准备迎接巴库站在本周末阿塞拜疆大奖赛期间暴露2026年赛车需要更多“极其不自然”驾驶方式的问题。
巴库提供了独特的挑战，因为它拥有赛历上最长的全油门路段（超过两公里长），但这给F1能量匮乏的2026年赛车带来了重大问题。
这意味着车手在排位赛中需要在起终点直道上部署大部分电池能量，导致他们在赛道其余部分动力极低，弯道出弯时出现巨大的功率差异。
“这会很有趣，因为你有两三条独特的直道需要部署大量动力，然后你在中间路段大部分时间都以非常非常低的功率运行，因为在那些超短直道上部署任何能量都非常低效，”哈斯车手奥利·贝尔曼解释道。
“你倾向于把能量留给通往1号弯、3号弯的较长直道。这意味着动力输出存在巨大差异。你出2号弯驶向3号弯时，有1000马力或无论多少，最大马力，然后出3号弯时只有大约三分之二，因为那是一条很短的直道，所以突然你的油门踏板只有前一个弯道一半的动力。
“所以这是非常奇怪的事情。它发生在某些赛道上，尤其是能量匮乏的赛道，但只在有短直道的特定区域。
“我们在蒙扎第二个减速弯（通往莱斯莫弯）之后遇到过，而在这里，每条短直道之间你都有非常低的功率。
“这意味着这真的很奇怪，因为你可以想象你在中间路段做一件事，然后突然你出另一个弯，动力翻倍。
“这对我们来说极其不自然；在今年二月之前，我们从未有过这种情况。”
车手对此无法控制，正如贝尔曼所说，“你只是踩油门踏板、刹车和转向，一切都会自行处理。我们在驾驶时实际上做的任何事情都不一定能影响它”。
车手以尽可能接近100%的电量到达起终点直道将至关重要——否则在排位赛和正赛中都将付出高昂代价。
正如皮埃尔·加斯利所解释的，“如果你没有100%，你只会更早开始削功率，但在这里更早不是200米，当你以低几公里/小时的速度持续那么长时间时，就开始变得相当昂贵了。
“从比赛角度来看，这种直道上有时你看到的不仅仅是一辆车经过，所以我绝对建议处于车群前列，尤其是在比赛日。
“但现实是我们无法控制所有这些方面。这是软件、各种因素、事故、条件等等，有时让我们处于有利或不利的一面，所以我们必须看看，但可以肯定的是，保持良好状态很重要。”
起终点线距1号弯不到200米，这意味着准备圈的车手在16号左弯出弯后的大部分路段将仅依靠内燃机动力。
从16号左弯出弯开始有1250米的时段，车手可以避免功率下降率并减少350千瓦功率，这意味着他们将仅靠内燃机动力行驶。还有类似的时段，如果他们愿意，可以从3号弯一直到12号弯纯靠内燃机动力行驶。
相比之下，正在飞驰圈的车手一旦进入主直道就会部署大部分能量，因此正如车手们已经警告的那样，可能会出现一些极端的接近速度。
“开始圈的车手非常慢，直到电池在起终点线前介入，”费尔南多·阿隆索说。
“大约有20秒你会以200公里/小时行驶，而其他人以350公里/小时冲过来。
“无法移动，尤其是在18-19号弯（全油门弯道）。所以这将是本周末的挑战之一：确保我们安全，在车手简报会上，我们选择移动的位置。”
奥迪的加布里埃尔·博尔托莱托预测，“这会有点混乱，尤其是我们在飞驰圈离开最后一个弯时速度那么快，而开始圈的车手会那么慢。
“所以希望这不会危险。希望我们在18号和19号弯能做些事情，因为我想如果你以我不知道300公里/小时左右的速度冲过来，而另一辆车以250公里/小时行驶，因为没有MGU-K在部署，那可能会很危险。”
当被问及是否会在周四的车手简报会上讨论时，博尔托莱托说：“是的，但他们打算怎么做呢？”
巴库的主要挑战之一是环绕赛道的建筑物之间流动的风，它每一圈、每个弯道都在变化。周五排位赛还预报有39公里/小时的大风。
弗兰科·科拉平托说：“我认为风会很棘手；去年我们因为风看到了很多红旗。它变化得像疯了一样——阵风，因为建筑物。
“你会遇到五秒钟的阵风，然后五秒钟没有，然后又来。它太不稳定了，对我们来说非常困难，尤其是在街道赛道上。
“这让比赛更加棘手，更加危险。”
赛车公牛车手阿尔维德·林德布拉德不太确定：“我认为在今年赛车上这不是大问题，因为它们对空气动力学不那么敏感”。不过我相信这仍然是个问题。
detailEn: Formula 1 drivers are braced for Baku to expose the requirement for more "super unnatural" driving of the 2026 cars during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix this weekend.
Baku provides a unique challenge as it possesses the longest flat-out run on the calendar (over two kilometres long), but that creates major problems for F1's energy-starved 2026 cars.

It means drivers will need to deploy most of their battery on the start/finish straight in qualifying, leaving them with very little power around the rest of the lap and some huge power disparities on corner exits.

"‘It's going to be interesting because you have two or three distinctive straights where you have to deploy a lot of power and then you spend a lot of the middle sector running with really, really low power because it's very inefficient to deploy any energy in those super short straights," Haas driver Ollie Bearman explained.

"You tend to save it for the longer ones into Turn 1, into Turn 3. It means that you have a massive disparity in power delivery. You come out of Turn 2 heading into Turn 3 and you have a thousand horsepower or however much, maximum horsepower and then you have like two-thirds of that coming out of Turn 3 because it's a really short straight, so suddenly your throttle pedal is half as powerful as it was in the previous corner.
"So it's a really strange thing. It happens in some circuits, especially the energy-starved ones, but it's only in specific areas where there's short straights.
"We had it in Monza out of the second chicane [towards the Lesmos], here between every short straight you have really low power.
"It means that it's really strange because you can imagine you spend the middle sector doing one thing and then suddenly you come out of another corner and you have twice as much power.
"It's super unnatural for us; we've never had that before ever until February this year."

Drivers have no control over this, as Bearman says, "you just press the throttle pedal and brake and steer, and it all takes care of itself. There's nothing we actually do whilst driving that can necessarily affect it".
It's going to be crucial for drivers to arrive at the start/finish straight with as close to 100% battery as possible - or it will be very costly in both qualifying and the race.

As Pierre Gasly explained, "if you don't have 100%, "You're just going to start clipping earlier, but earlier here is not 200 metres [and] when you're down a couple of km/h for that long, then it starts to be quite costly.
"Racing-wise, it's the type of straight where sometimes you don't only see one car passing by, so I would definitely recommend to be top of the pack, especially when it comes to race day.

"But the reality is we don't have control of all of that side. It's software, it's whatever, incidents, conditions, etc that sometimes leads us to being on the right side of it or the wrong side of it, so we'll have to see, but for sure, it's important to be fine."

The start/finish line being located less than 200 metres from Turn 1 means drivers on a preparation lap will be relying solely on internal combustion engine power for the majority of the run out of the Turn 16 left-hander.

There's a 1250 metre period beginning at the exit of the Turn 16 left-hander where drivers can avoid a ramp-down rate and drop 350kw of power, meaning they'll just be on internal combustion engine power. And a similar period where they can do the same and run purely on ICE power from Turn 3 all the way to Turn 12 if they wish to do so.
In contrast, those drivers on a lap will be deploying most of their energy once on the main straight, so there's the potential for some extreme closing speeds as drivers have already warned.
"People opening the lap are very slow until the battery comes in just before the line," Fernando Alonso said.
"There are like 20 seconds that you will be at 200km/h, and people are coming at 350[km/h].

"There is no way to move, especially in Turn 18-19 [flat-out kinked corners]. So that will be one of the challenges of the weekend: to make sure that we are safe, on the drivers' briefing, and we choose the places where to move."
Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto predicted, "it's going to be a bit of a mess, especially as we are leaving the last corner in a push lap so quickly, and then people opening the laps are going to be so slow.

"So hopefully that's not going to be dangerous. Hopefully there is going to be something that we can do in that Turn 18 and Turn 19 corners, because I guess it can be dangerous if you are coming at I don't know 300km/h and something, and another car is at 250km/h because there is no MGU-K being deployed."
Asked if it will be discussed at the drivers' briefing on Thursday, Bortoleto said: "Yeah, but what are they going to do about it?"

One of Baku's staple challenges is the wind that flows between the buildings that surround the circuit and changes lap after lap and corner after corner. There are also 39km/h winds forecast for qualifying on Friday.
Franco Colapinto said "I think the wind is going to be tricky; last year we saw a lot of red flags because of the wind. It was changing like crazy - the gusts, because of the buildings.
"You'd get it for five seconds and the five seconds after, no gust, and then again. It was so inconsistent that it would be very difficult for us, especially on a street track.
"It makes it much more tricky and much more sketchy."
Racing Bulls driver Arvid Lindblad wasn't so sure: "I think that's less of a thing in this year's cars because they're less sensitive with the aero". I'm sure it's still a thing, though."
keyPointsZh: 巴库拥有赛历上最长的全油门路段（超过两公里），这对2026年能量匮乏的赛车构成重大挑战。
车手在排位赛中需在起终点直道部署大部分电池能量，导致赛道其余部分动力极低，弯道出弯功率差异巨大。
起终点线距1号弯不到200米，准备圈车手在16号弯出弯后大部分路段仅靠内燃机动力，与飞驰圈车手可能产生极端接近速度。
keyPointsEn: Baku has the longest flat-out run on the calendar (over two kilometres), creating major problems for F1's energy-starved 2026 cars.
Drivers will need to deploy most of their battery on the start/finish straight in qualifying, leaving very little power around the rest of the lap and huge power disparities on corner exits.

The start/finish line being less than 200 metres from Turn 1 means drivers on a preparation lap will rely solely on internal combustion engine power for most of the run out of Turn 16, potentially creating extreme closing speeds with drivers on a flying lap.

detailZh: F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛：周四赛程、天气预报及观看方式
2026年一级方程式阿塞拜疆大奖赛第一次自由练习和第二次自由练习的开始时间，以及巴库完整赛程、天气预报和直播观看方式
一级方程式本周前往巴库，迎接一个时间异常提前的阿塞拜疆大奖赛周末，所有赛道上的活动都提前了一天。
自由练习于周四开始，排位赛于周五进行，大奖赛正赛将于周六举行。之所以做出调整，是因为阿塞拜疆在9月27日星期日迎来纪念日（阵亡将士纪念日）。
基米·安东内利带着对积分榜的牢牢掌控抵达巴库，他刚刚赢得了最近两场比赛的胜利。随着阿塞拜疆迎来2026赛季第15站比赛，这位梅赛德斯车手目前领先队友乔治·拉塞尔81分。
今年也是一级方程式首次在巴库街道比赛10周年。这条赛道于2016年以欧洲大奖赛的名义加入赛历，次年成为阿塞拜疆大奖赛，其狭窄的街道路段与极长的主直道相结合，应该会再次使能量释放（部署）成为比赛议程上的重点。
周四将进行第一次自由练习，随后在下午晚些时候进行第二次自由练习。以下是在阿塞拜疆大奖赛开幕日之前你需要了解的一切。
一级方程式的转播覆盖因地区而异。对于英国的观众来说，天空体育继续作为该锦标赛的独家转播商，在2026赛季全程直播每一节比赛。F1的转播也可以通过天空的流媒体平台（Sky Go）或另一流媒体平台（NOW）观看，精彩集锦则可在第四频道免费收看到。
Motorsport.com 将在整个阿塞拜疆大奖赛周末提供实时报道和更新。

预计星期四巴库天气温和，大部分时间晴到局部多云，气温大约在22摄氏度到25摄氏度之间。
下雨的可能性不大，这应该能为车队在头两节练习赛中提供稳定的条件。风可能是更大的影响因素，来自里海的海风在穿过巴库较狭窄的赛段时，在建筑物之间可能变得更加明显。
预计星期五在最后一次练习赛和排位赛期间将保持干燥晴朗，不过更强的风力可能使比赛条件更加困难。
根据目前的预报，阿塞拜疆大奖赛周六天气晴朗，正赛开始时气温约为24摄氏度。

detailEn: F1 Azerbaijan GP: Thursday schedule, weather forecast and how to watch
What time free practice 1 and free practice 2 start at the 2026 Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, plus the full Baku schedule, weather forecast and how to watch live
Formula 1 heads to Baku this week for an unusually early Azerbaijan GP weekend, with all of the on-track action shifted forward by a day.

Free practice begins on Thursday, qualifying takes place on Friday and the grand prix itself will be held on Saturday. The change was requested because Azerbaijan marks Remembrance Day on Sunday, September 27.

Kimi Antonelli arrives in Baku firmly in control of the championship after winning the last two races. The Mercedes driver holds an 81-point advantage over team-mate George Russell with Azerbaijan hosting round 15 of the 2026 season.

This year also marks 10 years since Formula 1 first raced on the streets of Baku. The circuit joined the calendar as the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming the Azerbaijan GP the following year, and its combination of tight street sections and a very long main straight should once again put energy deployment high on the agenda.
Thursday brings free practice 1 followed by free practice 2 later in the afternoon. Here is everything you need to know ahead of the opening day of the Azerbaijan GP.

Broadcast coverage of Formula 1 varies by region. For viewers in the United Kingdom, Sky Sports continues as the championship’s exclusive broadcaster, showing every session live throughout the 2026 season. F1 coverage can also be streamed via Sky Go or NOW, with highlights available free-to-air on Channel 4.
Motorsport.com will provide live coverage and updates throughout the Azerbaijan GP weekend.

Thursday, September 24 — free practice 2 — 4:00pm AZT
Thursday, September 24 — free practice 1 — 9:30am BST
Thursday, September 24 — free practice 2 — 1:00pm BST
Thursday, September 24 — free practice 1 — 4:30am ET
Thursday, September 24 — free practice 2 — 8:00am ET
Thursday, September 24 — free practice 1 — 12:30pm AZT
Thursday, September 24 — free practice 2 — 4:00pm AZT
Friday, September 25 — free practice 3 — 12:30pm AZT
Friday, September 25 — qualifying — 4:00pm AZT
Saturday, September 26 — 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix — 3:00pm AZT
Thursday is expected to be mild and mostly sunny to partly cloudy in Baku, with temperatures between roughly 22C and 25C.

Rain is unlikely, which should give teams stable conditions for the opening two practice sessions. Wind could be a bigger factor, with breezes coming in from the Caspian Sea and potentially becoming more noticeable between the buildings through Baku’s narrower sections.
Friday is expected to remain dry and sunny for final practice and qualifying, although stronger winds could make conditions more difficult.
Saturday is currently forecast to be clear for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with temperatures around 24C at the start of the race.
Thursday sessions: free practice 1 and free practice 2
Friday sessions: free practice 3 and qualifying
Baku combines narrow street sections with a long run to the start-finish line, putting a premium on confidence under braking, straightline performance and energy management.
